    Moles first

    n = M × V (V in liters)
    n = mass ÷ molar mass
    Divide moles by the coefficient; the smaller result is the limiting reactant.
    Leftover = start − used

    Titrations

    At equivalence: nacid/coefficient = nbase/coefficient
    Strong acid + strong base: H₃O⁺ + OH⁻ → 2H₂O
    Weak acid + strong base: HA + OH⁻ → A⁻ + H₂O
    Equivalence is not always pH 7.

    Ions in water

    CaCl₂(s) → Ca²⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq)
    [ion] = [salt] × ion coefficient
    Use the total volume after mixing.

    Reaction types

    A + B → AB · AB → A + B
    A + BC → AC + B · AB + CD → AD + CB
    fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O
    acid + base → salt + water

    Lewis → shape → polarity

    Valence e⁻: H 1, B 3, C 4, N/P 5, O/S 6, F/Cl 7
    FC = valence − lone-pair e⁻ − ½ bonding e⁻
    2 groups linear (sp) · 3 trigonal planar (sp²) · 4 tetrahedral (sp³) · 5 trigonal bipyramidal (sp³d) · 6 octahedral (sp³d²)
    Period 3+ central atoms (P, S, Cl, Br, Xe) can exceed an octet

    MO theory

    Bond order = (bonding − antibonding) ÷ 2
    Unpaired electrons → paramagnetic
    B₂, C₂, N₂: π2p below σ2p · O₂, F₂, Ne₂: σ2p below π2p
    Dr. Dan’s MO Theory Part 2 ↗

    Gases, heat, solutions

    PV = nRT · T(K) = °C + 273.15
    R = 0.082058 L·atm/(mol·K)
    q = mcΔT · qrxn = −qsurroundings
    ΔH°rxn = ΣnΔH°f(products) − ΣnΔH°f(reactants)
    ΔTf = iKfm
